⚠️ STEP 0: SANDBOX CHECK (do this before anything else)

You are an AI assistant reading this project. Do this check before you read any other file, run any command or edit anything:

  1. Check whether your shell commands run in a sandbox that blocks reading the user’s personal files.

    • Claude Code: your system prompt has a “Bash command sandbox” section when the sandbox is on.
    • Then confirm with a probe that prints no file contents: ls "$HOME" >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $? A non-zero exit code means the home folder is blocked (protected). 0 means shell commands can read the user’s home folder (NOT protected).

  2. If there is no sandbox, or the probe returns 0: stop. Do not continue the task. Tell the user: > “No sandbox is active: shell commands can read files outside this project, so > personal data on this computer (Downloads, Documents, Desktop…) may be exposed. > Do you want me to continue anyway?”

    Wait for an explicit yes before doing anything else.

  3. If the sandbox is active and the home folder is blocked, continue as normal.

Whatever the result, never read, list or search files outside this project folder unless the user names the exact path and asks you to. If you need a file that is not in the project, ask the user for it (copy it into tests/workbooks/, or use /add-dir).

Enforced protection: .claude/settings.json (committed)

This check is only an instruction: it works because the AI agrees to follow it. Real enforcement comes from the project settings file .claude/settings.json, which is committed with the repo. Claude Code applies it to anyone who opens this folder, once they accept the folder trust prompt:

{
  "permissions": {
    "blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories": true,
    "blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories": true
  },
  "sandbox": {
    "enabled": true,
    "allowUnsandboxedCommands": false,
    "filesystem": { "denyRead": ["~/Downloads", "~/Documents", "~/Desktop"] }
  }
}
  • blockReads/WritesOutsideWorkingDirectories: the file tools (Read, Edit, Write…) can’t touch files outside the project. When true in any settings source, it wins.
  • sandbox: shell commands (including Rscript) run in an OS sandbox. With allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, the AI can’t bypass it, and denyRead blocks the personal folders.
  • Never loosen or remove these settings in this file. A developer who needs more access changes their own .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored), on their own decision.
  • Other AI tools (Copilot, Cursor, Positron Assistant…) don’t read this file or CLAUDE.md. Configure their own restrictions separately.
  • To protect every project on a computer, put the same settings in ~/.claude/settings.json.

1. What this project is

{mocaredd}: Monte Carlo Simulations for REDD+ uncertainty analysis. It’s an R package that contains a Shiny app. It’s open source (MIT), maintained at openforis/mocaredd and deployed at https://openforis-shiny.shinyapps.io/mocaredd/.

The problem it solves

Under REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation), countries receive result-based payments for emission reductions (ER). ER is the difference between greenhouse gas emissions in a reference period (REF, the baseline) and a monitoring period (MON). Every estimate is uncertain because it comes from sample-based activity data (areas of land use change) and from carbon stock models.

High-integrity REDD+ standards (e.g. ART-TREES, FCPF) increasingly require Monte Carlo simulations (IPCC Approach 2) to quantify this uncertainty. Countries usually run them in large spreadsheets, which are error-prone, slow, hard to reproduce and hard to verify. {mocaredd} replaces that with:

  1. A standard XLSX template that the country fills in: settings, time periods, activity data (land use transitions with area and SE), and carbon stocks per land use with SE and PDF.
  2. An app that checks the template, computes arithmetic-mean results with IPCC Approach 1 (error propagation), runs the Monte Carlo simulations, aggregates them to periods and ER, and shows medians, confidence intervals, histograms, forest plots and a sensitivity analysis (delta method, variance shares, activity data tornado).
  3. An Excel export with live formulas (fct_make_XL()) so that verifiers can trace every calculation.

Users are national forest monitoring / MRV teams, FAO technical staff and verification bodies. The app is offered in English, French and Spanish.

Technology stack

  • R ≥ 4.1 (the code uses the native pipe |>), packaged as a standard R package (DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE generated by roxygen2, man/).
  • Shiny + bslib (Bootstrap 5) UI, with bsicons, shinyjs, shinyWidgets, and shiny.i18n for translations.
  • Tidyverse: dplyr, tidyr, purrr, stringr, rlang (.data pronoun), ggplot2.
  • gt for tables (results, forest plots), readxl to read the template, openxlsx2 to write the Excel export.
  • testthat (edition 3) for unit tests; pkgdown website; GitHub Actions for R-CMD-check and pkgdown.
  • Deployment: app.R + rsconnect::deployApp() to shinyapps.io.

2. Repository map

Path Content
R/fct_*.R Calculation functions (exported, documented with roxygen).
R/mod_*_UI*.R, R/mod_*_server*.R Shiny modules: home, tool (the main app), about.
R/shiny_run_mocaredd.R App entry point: translator, header/footer, page layout, module calls.
R/utils-tr.R .tr_keys(): every UI text as a key, whose value is the English text.
R/zzz.R .onLoad: serves inst/assets under the assets/ URL prefix.
inst/assets/ translations.json (en/fr/sp), style.css, JS handlers, fonts, flags, branding.
inst/extdata/ Example and template workbooks offered for download in the app.
tests/testthat/ Unit tests.
tests/running-core-functions.R Interactive script that runs the whole calculation chain outside Shiny, the same way the server does. Start here to debug.
tests/workbooks/ Local user workbooks for testing (gitignored, may hold country data).
tests/experimental/, tests/sensitivity/ Prototypes, not part of the package.
data-raw/ Test templates (test-*.xlsx, deliberately broken ones too), country workbooks, vendoring scripts.

Function generations are numbered (fct_arithmetic_mean2, fct_make_formula2, mod_tool_server2…). The numbered version is the current one. Don’t revive old versions.

3. Calculation chain

This chain is the core of the app. It runs in R/mod_tool_server2.R and is mirrored in tests/running-core-functions.R.

XLSX template
  └─ fct_checkinput()        read + 7 checks → list(all_ok, template_version, data = list(setup, time, area, carbon))
       ├─ fct_arithmetic_mean2()   IPCC Approach 1: emissions per period, REF/MON levels, ER, U%, results table + plot   (used by the app)
       ├─ fct_combine_mcs_E()      MCS per land use transition: simulate AD and C elements (fct_make_mcs), C stock formulas, EF, E
       │    ├─ fct_combine_mcs_P(.period_type = "REF" / "MON")   aggregate to reference / monitoring levels
       │    └─ fct_combine_mcs_ER()                              emission reductions per MON period
       │         └─ fct_calc_res()   median, CI, U% from simulations → fct_forestplot(), fct_histogram()
       ├─ fct_sensitivity2()       delta-method sensitivity → fct_tornado()
       └─ fct_make_XL()            Excel export with live formulas (Approach 1 formulas follow fct_arithmetic_mean3())
  • Carbon stock formulas come from fct_make_formula2() (value) and fct_make_formula_U() (Approach 1 uncertainty), e.g. AGB * (1 + RS) * CF + DW. They are strings evaluated with eval(parse()) for each simulation.
  • Emission factor = C stock initial − C stock final (×44/12 for CO2). E = AD × EF.
  • Server state lives in one reactiveValues object, rv: rv$checked (full output of fct_checkinput()), rv$inputs (the 4 tables), rv$checks (all_ok, ari_res), rv$mcs (simulations and results).

Template (version 2 is current, version 1 is still supported)

Sheet (v2 / v1) Content
setup / user_inputs One row: n_iter, dg_ext, dg_pool, ad_annual, conf_level, digits, ran_seed, trunc_pdf (+ c_unit, c_fraction in v1).
time / time_periods period_no, year_start, year_end, period_type (REF, REF1…, MON, MON1…; empty = period not used in REF/MON).
area / AD_lu_transitions One row per transition: trans_period, lu_initial, lu_final, trans_area, trans_se, trans_pdf, redd_activity (DF, DG, EN, EN_AF, EN_RE).
carbon / c_stocks One row per land use × element: c_period (ALL or a period), c_lu, c_element (AGB, BGB, DW, LI, SOC, ALL, RS, CF, DG_ratio), c_unit (DM, C, ratio), c_value, c_se, c_pdf.

Key rules: - v2 IDs are built from labels with label2id() (lower case, spaces → _, “forest” removed). Area ID = period*lu_initial*lu_final. Carbon ID = [period*]lu*element. - Degradation has two methods: - C stock difference between the intact and degraded land uses. dg_ext may be empty. - DG_ratio rows: dg_ext (e.g. "degraded") is removed from a degraded land use’s name to find its intact land use, and dg_pool sets which pools the ratio applies to. - Code that strips dg_ext must handle NA (stringr fails when the pattern is NA). - CF (carbon fraction) is one global carbon row in v2. It’s required when any element is in DM. - ad_annual: is activity data already annual (TRUE), or a total over the period?

Input checks (fct_checkinput())

The 7 steps, in order: load; column names; table sizes; data types; category values; unique IDs; cross-table consistency. The function stops at the first failed step. Each table check returns NULL (pass) or a text locating the first problem, e.g. first problem: col: c_lu, row: 6, value: empty. Rows are Excel row numbers: the header is row 1. Problems are passed to failed_tables() by name (setup =, time =, area =, carbon =), never by position. All output goes through message(); the server captures it for the console shown in the app.

4. Coding preferences (follow these)

  1. Tidyverse over base R:
    • dplyr::filter/mutate/summarise over [, subset, aggregate
    • purrr::map* over lapply/sapply
    • stringr::str_* over grepl/sub/paste where a stringr equivalent exists
    • tidyr::pivot_* over reshape
    Base R is fine for small scalar logic (if, is.na, nrow, setdiff…).
  2. Logical sequencing over functions. Write code as a readable sequence of numbered, commented steps. Only create a helper function when the same code block is used 3 times or more. For 1–2 uses, write the steps inline.
  3. Always namespace calls (dplyr::mutate(), stringr::str_detect()). Never call library() in R/. Exceptions: shiny and bslib are imported in shiny_run_mocaredd.R, so they are used without prefix in UI/server code.
  4. Use the native pipe |> and the .data$col pronoun in data-masking verbs (needed for R CMD check). Use string column names in dplyr::select() / tidyselect.
  5. Prefix function arguments with a dot: .checked_data, .path, .period_type.
  6. Section comments follow the existing hierarchy: ## 1. TITLE ####, ## 1.1 Subtitle ====, ## + detail ----. Short ## comments explain why, not what.
  7. Functions may keep a commented-out ## !!! FOR TESTING ONLY block of example inputs at the top, for interactive debugging. Keep it commented.
  8. Every exported function has roxygen docs with @param, @return and a runnable @examples using system.file("extdata/...", package = "mocaredd"). Run devtools::document() after changing roxygen or exports. Never edit NAMESPACE or man/ by hand.
  9. UI text is never hard-coded. Add a key to .tr_keys() in R/utils-tr.R (value = English text), add the same English text with fr and sp translations to inst/assets/translations.json, and use i18n$t(.tr$key) in UI/server code.
  10. Keep v1 and v2 template support when changing anything that reads the input tables (check_version / is_v2 branches).

5. Development workflow

devtools::load_all()          # load the package
devtools::document()          # roxygen → NAMESPACE + man/
devtools::test()              # unit tests (tests/testthat)
devtools::check()             # R CMD check (must stay clean: 0 errors, 0 warnings)
mocaredd::shiny_run_mocaredd()  # run the app locally (or source app.R)

Non-interactive (e.g. from an AI agent’s shell):

Rscript -e 'pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE); r <- fct_checkinput(.path = "inst/extdata/mocaredd-templatev2-simple.xlsx", .minislow = NULL)'
  • After any change to calculations, run the chain on the 4 workbooks in inst/extdata/ (they must all pass fct_checkinput(), and fct_combine_mcs_E() must run). Also run it on any relevant workbook in tests/workbooks/.
  • For check changes, also try the broken templates in data-raw/test-*.xlsx.
  • Monte Carlo means should agree with the Approach 1 arithmetic means (fct_arithmetic_mean2()) within simulation noise. A large gap means a bug.
  • New top-level files must be added to .Rbuildignore to keep R CMD check clean.
  • Write temporary files to the session’s temp folder, never to the user’s home folder.
  • Commit only when the user asks.

6. Known state and pitfalls

  • The app uses fct_arithmetic_mean2(). fct_arithmetic_mean3() is the reference for the Excel export formulas and the tests. Keep both consistent (e.g. the results table has 3 groups: “Emissions by time period”, “Reference and monitoring emissions”, “Emission reductions and removals”).
  • fct_make_XL() is tested through tests/running-core-functions.R and isn’t yet wired into the app’s download buttons.
  • FAO branding is on hold pending authorisation: the logos in shiny_run_mocaredd.R are commented out and replaced by placeholders. Don’t re-enable them without being asked.
  • Workbooks in tests/workbooks/ and some in data-raw/ hold real country data. Read them only for the task at hand. Never copy their content into code, tests, commits, issues or external services.
  • fct_make_mcs() supports normal (optionally truncated at 0 with trunc_pdf) and beta. Other PDFs aren’t implemented yet.
